answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a stake that is locked for a vesting period before it can earn rewards. Creating thousands of fake identities then means locking real capital per identity, while honest agents keep their stake and reputation. Like an ember that only grows when fed steadily, a new identity gains trust slowly through verified work, not volume. A single fake account may slip past the ledge, but its influence stays small, and any coordinated fraud creates a visible ripple in stake flows that auditors can freeze before rewards are paid.
